transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I feel like people aren’t listening to me. For months now I’ve been trying to get someone to understand that my husband’s family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. It’s not always obvious, that’s the thing—like little billing errors show up at work, or someone at church suddenly acts strange toward me, and everyone says it’s just a mistake or I’m reading too much into it.

But I know it ties back to them. Even when people pull up records and say everything looks normal, that doesn’t mean it is. They’re careful about it. And I’m tired of being treated like I’m making trouble when I’m the one trying to protect us.
Do you think your husband's family is actively working against you?

Yes, I do. I mean, not like they’d come out and say it, of course. It’s quiet, it’s little things. For months I’ve been trying to get people to see it—our money, our name, the way people look at me.

Like at work, I do billing, so I know when something is off, and these little errors start showing up. And then someone at church acts funny toward me, like they’ve heard something. My sister-in-law always did have a way of smiling when she meant something else—sorry, that’s not really the point, but it’s that kind of thing.

People keep saying the records look fine, or it’s just coincidence, but I know it ties back to his family. They’re careful. That’s why it’s hard to prove.
Do you think anyone else believes that your husband's family is working against you?

Some people believe me a little, I think, or at least they can tell something’s not right. But then when they look at records, they say, “Well, everything seems normal,” like that settles it. It doesn’t.

My husband… he doesn’t really want to talk about it. He gets uncomfortable, and then I feel like I’m the only one willing to look at the pattern. Because it’s not just one thing—it’s the little billing errors at work, and then someone at church treating me differently, and you know, people can ruin your name without ever saying anything straight to your face. His family is careful that way.

So, do other people believe it? Not the way they should. But I know it ties back to them.
Do you think your husband's family is actually capable of pulling off something like this without anyone noticing?

Yes, I think they are. People act like something has to be dramatic for it to be real, but it’s not like that. It’s quiet things—little billing errors where I work, someone at church suddenly looking at me different, like they’ve heard something.

And my husband’s family, they know how to do things without putting their name on it. That’s the whole point. My sister-in-law, she’s always been the kind who can say one thing and mean another—well, anyway, I know that sounds like I’m getting off track. But yes, I do think they’re capable, because every time someone pulls up a record and says it looks normal, it still doesn’t explain why these things keep happening and why it always seems to tie back to them.
Have you ever had a period of time where you didn't think your husband's family was working against you?

Before that? I mean… yes, I suppose I didn’t always think that way. It’s really been about nine months now.

It started after that trouble with his family over money, and then the holiday expectations—who was supposed to pay for what, where we were supposed to be, all of that. Families make such a big production out of holidays, and then if you don’t do exactly what they want, suddenly you’re the difficult one.

But before all that, no, I wasn’t sitting around thinking they were working against me. It’s been since then that I started seeing how things were lining up.
Have you ever considered the possibility that your husband's family might not be working against you?

I’ve considered it in the way people keep telling me to consider it, yes. I’m not unreasonable. I know records can look normal, and I know someone can say, “Well, where’s the proof?” But that doesn’t mean it isn’t happening.

I mean, I’m here because for months I’ve been trying to get people to understand that his family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. It’s little things, not some big scene—billing errors showing up where I work, and then someone at church suddenly acting funny toward me. And church used to be one place where I could just sit and not feel judged, you know, but now even there it feels different.

So… could I say the words, “maybe they’re not”? I suppose. But when I look at the pattern, I don’t believe that. No matter what records anyone pulls up, I know it ties back to them.
Have you ever changed your mind about your husband's family working against you, even if only for a short time?

Not really changed my mind, no. I mean, there are moments when I’m tired of talking about it and I think, fine, maybe I should just let it go for an afternoon. Like at church, if someone smiles normally, I’ll think maybe it’s not so bad, but then later someone acts strange or there’s another little billing thing at work, and it all starts lining up again.

And it’s not like I want to believe this. I’m here because for months I’ve been trying to get people to understand that his family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. People keep saying the records look normal, but that doesn’t explain why these things keep happening. So no, I haven’t really changed my mind. Maybe I’ve tried to set it aside, but I still know it ties back to them.
Do you think there's any possibility, no matter how small, that you could be mistaken about your husband's family working against you?

I mean… I guess anything is possible in the way people say that. Like, sure, maybe I could misunderstand one person looking at me funny at church, because people have bad days, and church coffee hour is always awkward anyway—someone’s casserole, someone’s grandkids, all that.

But when it keeps happening, when the little billing errors show up at work and then people start treating me differently, and it’s tied in with my husband’s family and the way they’ve been about money and reputation… I don’t think I’m mistaken. No matter what records anybody pulls up, I know it goes back to them somehow.
Have you ever had a time, even briefly, where you doubted your belief that your husband's family is working against you?

Briefly? Maybe a flicker, like when I’m busy at work and just trying to get the postings done and someone says, “Oh, it was just a mistake,” and for a second I think, fine, maybe that one thing was just a mistake.

But then it’s never just one thing, is it? It’s the little billing errors, and then somebody at church suddenly acts like they’ve heard something about me, and you start putting it together. My husband’s family has been quietly messing with our money and our good name for months, and people keep acting like if the records look normal then that settles it. It doesn’t.

So I wouldn’t say I really doubt it. I might get tired of carrying it around, or I might try not to think about it while I’m making dinner or sitting through service, but underneath that I still know it ties back to them.
Do you think your belief about your husband's family working against you has ever wavered at all?

Wavered… I don’t know if I’d call it that. I get worn down, you know, and sometimes I try to think about something else—like I’ll be at church and someone is talking about the bake sale or whose son is visiting, and for a minute I think, maybe I’m making too much of one look or one comment.

But then the same kinds of things happen again. The little billing errors at work, people acting funny toward me, and it all points back to my husband’s family. I’m here because for months I’ve been trying to get people to understand they’re quietly messing with our money and our good name. People can pull up whatever records they want and say it looks normal, but that doesn’t change what I know. So… no, not really wavered. Maybe I get tired, but I still know it ties back to them.
Have you ever thought that other people, outside of your husband's family, are working against you?

Other people… I mean, people get pulled into things, don’t they? Like at church, somebody suddenly acts funny toward me, or at work those little billing errors show up and everyone looks at me like I’m the problem.

But I don’t think it starts with just random people. It ties back to my husband’s family. That’s what I’ve been trying to explain for months—they’re quietly messing with our money and our good name. And then other people pick up on it, or they hear something, or they act differently. You can pull up records and say everything looks normal, but that doesn’t mean it isn’t connected.
Has there ever been a time when you didn't think about your husband's family working against you for an entire day?

An entire day? I don’t think so. I mean, I’m busy sometimes—at work there’s postings to get through, and then dinner, church things, whatever needs doing around the house—but it’s sort of always there in the back of my mind.

Because for months I’ve been trying to get people to understand this isn’t just me being sensitive. My husband’s family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. Like those little billing errors that show up, or someone at church suddenly acting strange with me, and then people say, “Well, the records look normal,” like that proves anything.

So maybe I don’t sit and think about it every single minute, but a whole day without it crossing my mind? No. It ties back to them, and once you see that, you don’t just forget it.
Do you ever have moments where you are completely certain that your husband's family is not working against you?

Completely certain they’re not? No, I can’t say I have that. I mean, sometimes I’m washing dishes or doing the church bulletin stuff and I think, oh, maybe I should just let it go for the evening, you know, because you get tired of carrying it around.

But then I remember why I’m here in the first place. For months I’ve been trying to get people to understand that my husband’s family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. It’s not one big dramatic thing—it’s little billing errors at work, or someone at church suddenly acting funny with me. And people can pull up records and say, “See, it looks normal,” but that doesn’t change what I know. It ties back to them. So no, I don’t really have moments where I’m certain they’re not doing it.
Do you think your beliefs about your husband's family working against you might be considered unreasonable by others?

I suppose they might say that, yes. People do say things like, “That doesn’t make sense,” or “The records look fine,” and then I’m the one standing there looking like I’m making trouble.

But I’m here because for months now I’ve been trying to get people to understand that my husband’s family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. It’s not like I’m saying something wild just to say it. It’s the little billing errors showing up, and then someone at church acts funny toward me, and it all… it all fits together if you’re paying attention.

Other people may call it unreasonable because they don’t see the whole picture. Or they don’t want to. But I know it ties back to them.
Do you think there's anything that could ever convince you that your husband's family is not working against you?

I don’t know what could convince me, honestly. People keep saying, “Well, the records look normal,” like that’s supposed to settle it, but records can look normal and still… things can be going on underneath.

I mean, I’m here because for months I’ve been trying to get people to understand that his family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. It’s not one big thing you can point to with a spotlight on it. It’s those little billing errors that show up, and then at church someone who used to be perfectly friendly suddenly acts strange, won’t quite look me in the eye, and you start thinking, okay, where did that come from?

And my husband—well, he’ll say I’m connecting things, but then he doesn’t sit at my desk all day seeing the postings, and he doesn’t hear the tone people use at fellowship after service. So could something convince me? Maybe if everything stopped and people admitted what they’d been doing. But just showing me records and saying it’s fine? No. I know it ties back to them.
Have you ever considered seeking a second opinion about the issues you're experiencing with your husband's family?

A second opinion… well, I guess that’s partly why I’m here, isn’t it? Though I don’t really see it as needing an “opinion” exactly, because this has been going on for months.

I’ve tried to get people to understand that my husband’s family is quietly interfering with our money and our reputation. Like at work, I’ll see these little billing errors show up, and people act like it’s just a mistake, but I know how postings are supposed to look. I’ve done that kind of work long enough. And then at church, someone will suddenly be odd with me, like they’ve heard something, and I think, well, that didn’t come from nowhere.

People can pull up records and say everything looks fine, but that doesn’t mean it is. So yes, I came here, but I don’t need someone to just tell me I’m imagining it. I need someone to understand how it all ties back to them.
Do you think there is any evidence that could ever change your mind about your husband's family working against you?

I mean… evidence is a funny word, because people keep acting like if the paper looks clean, then nothing happened. But I work with billing and postings, I know little things can be moved around and made to look like an error.

So if you ask what could change my mind… I don’t know. Maybe if the billing mistakes stopped, and people at church stopped treating me like they’d heard some story about me, and his family just stayed out of our business for once. But every time someone pulls up records and says, “See, it’s fine,” that doesn’t answer why these things keep happening.

I’ve been trying for months to get people to see it. They’re quietly messing with our money and our good name, and it all ties back to them.
Have you ever considered that your husband's family might actually be innocent and that you're misinterpreting their actions?

I’ve considered it because people keep asking me that, but… no, I don’t think I’m just misreading it. I know how that sounds, but when you keep seeing little billing errors show up, and then at church someone suddenly acts funny with you, like they’ve heard something, it’s hard to pretend it’s all coincidence.

And it’s not like I wanted this. I used to get along fine, mostly. I mean, families have their issues—my aunt used to say in-laws always smile at the table and talk in the kitchen, and maybe that stuck with me—but this has been months now. I’m here because I’ve been trying to get people to understand that my husband’s family is quietly messing with our money and our good name.

People can pull up whatever records they want and say, “See, nothing’s there,” but that doesn’t change what I’m seeing. It ties back to them.
Do you think your belief about your husband's family working against you could be a mistaken idea that you've become very attached to?

I don’t think it’s just some mistaken idea I got attached to. I know people keep trying to put it that way, like I’m holding onto it for no reason, but I’m here because for months I’ve been trying to get someone to understand what’s happening.

It’s not one big obvious thing, it’s these little things. Billing errors showing up where they shouldn’t, and I know how those postings work. Then someone at church acts strange toward me, like something’s been said. And his family… they’re always around the edges of it somehow, quietly affecting our money and our good name.

I mean, my mother used to say you can tell when people are smiling to your face but doing something else behind your back, and that’s kind of what this feels like. So no, I don’t think it’s just because I’m attached to the idea. Records can look fine and still not show the whole story. I know it ties back to them.
